===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*lewbʰ-|id=love}}
From {{inh|en|enm|love}}, {{m|enm|luve}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lufu}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*lubu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*lubō}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*lewbʰ-|t=love, care, desire}}.

The ''close of a letter'' sense is presumably a truncation of ''With love'' or the like.

The verb is from {{inh|en|enm|loven}}, {{m|enm|luvien}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lufian|t=to love}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*lubōn|t=to love}}, derived from the noun.

Eclipsed non-native {{noncog|en|amour|t=love}}, borrowed from {{noncog|nrf|amour|t=love}}.
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|sco|luve|t=love}}, {{cog|stq|ljo}}, {{m|stq|ljoo}}, {{m|stq|ljoof|t=dear, sweet}}, {{m|stq|Ljoote}}, {{m|stq|Ljoowe|t=love}}, {{cog|fy|leaf|t=friendly, kind, cordial}}, {{m|fy|leafde|t=love}}, {{cog|nl|lief|t=lovely, nice, sweet}}, {{m|nl|liefde|t=love}}, {{cog|de|lieb|t=dear; lovable}}, {{m|de|Liebe|t=love}}, {{cog|nds-de|Leevde}}, {{m|nds-de|Lieve|t=love}}, {{cog|lb|léif|t=lovely, kind, nice, sweet}}, {{m|lb|Léift|t=love}}, {{cog|wym|łiwa|t=love}}, {{cog|yi|ליב|t= nice; kind}}, {{cog|is|ljúfur|t=beloved, dear}}, {{cog|nn|-}}, {{cog|sv|ljuv|t=lovely, sweet}}, {{cog|got|𐌻𐌹𐌿𐍆𐍃|t=beloved, dear}}, {{cog|sq|lyp|t=to beg}}, {{cog|ru|любовь|t=love}}, {{cog|lt|liaupsė|t=praise}}, {{cog|la|libido|t=desire, lust}}, {{cog|pl|lubić|t=to like}}, {{cog|fa|آلفتن|tr=âloftan|t=to enamor}}, {{cog|sa|लोभ|t=desire, greed}}.
{{col-bottom}}

====Noun====
[[Image:DickseeRomeoandJuliet.jpg|thumb|Romeo and Juliet in love]]
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|uncountable}} A [[deep]] [[care|caring]] for the [[existence]] of another.
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[strong|Strong]] [[affection]].
#: {{ant|en|hate|hatred|angst|indifference}}
## A [[profound]] and caring [[affection]] towards someone.
##: {{ux|en|A mother’s '''love''' is not easily shaken.}}
##: {{ux|en|My husband’s '''love''' is the most important thing in my life.}}
##: {{ux|en|My '''love''' for Melca is eternal.}}
##* {{quote-text|en|year=1674|author=w:John Milton|title=w:Paradise Lost
|passage=He on his side / Leaning half-raised, with looks of cordial '''love''' / Hung over her enamoured.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2014|author=S. Hidden|title=Jewish, Christian, and Islamic Mystical Perspectives on the '''Love''' of God|isbn=1137443324}}
## [[affectionate|Affectionate]], [[benevolent]] [[concern]] or [[care]] for other [[people]] or [[being]]s, and for their [[well-being]].
##* '''1864''', ''Utilitarianism Explained and Exemplified in Moral and Political Government''<!-- 2014 reprint:({{ISBN|1108071422}}-->:
##*: The '''love''' of your neighbor as yourself, is expressly given as the definition and test of Charity,—not alms-giving—and this '''love''' is [...] the highest of all the Divine commands[.]<!--the work's later "love of God" seems like sense 1.1 instead-->
##* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1963
|author=[[w:Martin Luther King Jr.|Martin Luther King, Jr.]]
|chapter=A Tough Mind and a Tender Heart
|title=w:Strength to Love
|url=https://archive.org/details/strengthtolove00king/
|location=[[New York]]
|publisher=w:Pocket Books
|year_published=1964
|OCLC=768659813
|page=7
|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/strengthtolove00king/page/7/
|text=Through nonviolent resistance we shall be able to oppose the unjust system and at the same time '''love''' the perpetrators of the system. We must work passionately and unrelentingly for full stature as citizens, but may it never be said, my friends, that to gain it we used the inferior methods of falsehood, malice, hate, and violence.}}
## A [[feeling]] of [[intense]] [[attraction]] towards someone.
##: {{ux|en|I have never been in '''love''' as much as I have with you.}}
##* {{RQ:Congreve Mourning Bride|page=39|passage=Heav'n has no Rage, like '''Love''' to Hatred turn'd, / Nor Hell a Fury, like a Woman ſcorn'd.}}
##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=The humor of my proposition appealed more strongly to Miss Trevor than I had looked for, and from that time forward she became her old self again; for, even after she had conquered her '''love''' for the Celebrity, the mortification of having been jilted by him remained.}}
## A deep or [[abiding]] [[liking]] for something; an [[enthusiasm]] for something.
##: {{ux|en|My '''love''' of cricket knows no bounds.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Philip Auerswald|title=The Coming Prosperity|isbn=0199930848
|passage=For three decades, the average number of miles driven by US motorists increased steadily. Then, in 2007, that steady climb was suddenly halted. [...] What magic caused Americans to temper their longstanding '''love''' of the open road?}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} A person who is the object of [[romantic]] feelings; a [[darling]], a [[sweetheart]], a [[beloved]].
#: {{syn|en|baby|darling|honey|lover|pet|sweetheart|Thesaurus:sweetheart}}
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1595|author=w:Edmund Spenser|title=s:Epithalamion
|passage=Open the temple gates unto my '''love'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|III|2|text=O '''love''', dispatch all business, and be gone!}}
#* {{RQ:Haggard She|passage='Oh, my '''love''', my '''love'''!' she murmured, 'wilt thou ever know how I have loved thee?' and she kissed him on the forehead, and then went and stood in the pathway of the flame of Life.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1969|author=The Dubliners|title=Dirty Old Town|passage=I met my '''love''' by the gasworks wall.}}
# {{lb|en|colloquial|Commonwealth}} {{non-gloss|A term of friendly address, regardless of feelings.}}
#: {{syn|en|mate|darling|lovey|sweetie|sweetheart}}
#: {{ux|en|Hello '''love''', how can I help you?}}
# A thing, activity{{,}} etc. which is the object of one's deep liking or [[enthusiasm]].
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1997|month=March|title=Faces of Today's Black Woman|journal=Ebony|volume=52|issue=5|page=96
|passage=But it wasn't until [Theresa M. Claiborne] went to ROTC training camp at the University of California at Berkeley that she discovered that flying was her first '''love'''. "Pilots talk about getting bit by the flying bug," she says. "I thought, This is heaven."}}
# {{lb|en|euphemistic}} [[sexual|Sexual]] [[desire]]; [[attachment]] based on sexual [[attraction]].
#: {{syn|en|aphrodisia|carnality|Thesaurus:lust}}

# {{lb|en|euphemistic}} Sexual activity.
#: {{syn|en|lovemaking|sex|Thesaurus:copulation}}
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1986|author=Ben Elton; et al|title=w:Blackadder II|chapter=[[w:Bells (Blackadder)|Bells]]
|passage=—What think you, my lord, of... '''love'''?<br>—You mean ‘[[rumpy-pumpy]]’.}}
# An instance or episode of being [[in love]]; a [[love affair]].
#: {{syn|en|romance}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2014|author=E. L. Todd|title=Then Came Absolution|isbn=150282342X
|passage=Maybe it was just a summer '''love''', something with no future.}}
# {{non-gloss|Used as the [[closing]], before the [[signature]], of a [[letter]], especially between good friends or family members, or by the young.}}
# {{alt case|en|Love||personification of love}}.
#* {{circa|1810}}, Samuel Johnson (in ''The Works of Samuel Johnson''):
#*: At busy hearts in vain '''love's''' arrows fly; [...]

#* {{quote-text|en|year=1664|author=w:Robert Boyle|title=Experiments and Considerations Touching Colours,{{...}}
|passage=Such a kind of transparency, as that of a Sive, a piece of Cyprus, or a '''Love'''-Hood.}}
# A [[climb]]ing [[plant]], {{taxfmt|Clematis vitalba|species}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|usually|transitive|sometimes|_|intransitive|stative}} To have a strong [[affection]] for (someone or something).
#: {{ux|en|I '''love''' my spouse. &nbsp; [[I love you|I '''love''' you]]! &nbsp; I '''love''' that song!}}
#* {{RQ:Burroughs Land That Time Forgot||VI|passage= wanted to take her in my arms and tell her how I '''loved''' her, and had taken her hand from the rail and started to draw her toward me when Olson came blundering up on deck with his bedding.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=February 26 2013|author={{w|Pink (singer)|Pink}}; w:Nate Ruess|journal=w:Just Give Me a Reason
|passage=Just give me a reason, / just a little bit's enough, / just a second we're not broken, just bent / and we can learn to '''love''' again.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To need, [[thrive]] on.
#: {{ux|en|Mold '''loves''' moist, dark places.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To be strongly inclined towards something; an emphatic form of ''[[like]]''.
#: {{ux|en|I '''love''' walking barefoot on wet grass;&nbsp; I'd '''love''' to join the team;&nbsp; I '''love''' what you've done with your hair}}
#* {{RQ:Haggard She|passage="I '''love''' not that underlings should perceive my wisdom."}}
#* {{quote-book|1=en|year=1920|author=Agatha Christie|authorlink=Agatha Christie|title={{w|The Mysterious Affair at Styles}}|publisher=Pan Books|location=London|year_published=1954|page=141|passage=“Everywhere he went, I went with him. When I was twenty-three, I had been nearly all over the world. It was a splendid life—I '''loved''' it.”}}
# {{lb|en|usually|transitive|sometimes|_|intransitive}} To seek the good or honor of (someone), [[care]] deeply about, to be [[dedicated]] to (someone or something).
#* {{RQ:King James Version|John|3|16|text=For God so '''loued''' þe world, that he gaue his only begotten Sonne: that whosoeuer beleeueth in him, should not perish, but haue euerlasting life.}}
#* {{RQ:King James Version|Matthew|22|37|39|Iesus sayd vnto him, Thou shalt '''loue''' the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soule, and with all thy minde. This is the first and great Commandement. And the second is like vnto it, Thou shalt '''loue''' thy neighbour as thy selfe.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|sometimes|ironic}} To derive [[delight]] from a fact or situation.
#: {{ux|en|I '''love''' the fact that the coffee shop now offers fat-free chai latte.}}
# {{senseid|en|show approval of via a heart symbol}} {{lb|en|internet}} {{synonym of|en|heart<id:show approval of via a heart symbol><pos:verb>}}.
#: {{cot|en|like<id:show approval of via an online vote>|unlike#Verb}}
#: {{ux|en|She '''loved''' my photos of the kids playing with the dogs.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|euphemistic}} To [[sex|have sex]] with (perhaps from {{m|en|make love}}).
#: {{ux|en|I wish I could '''love''' her all night long.}}

===Etymology 2===
Now widely believed (due to historical written record) to be from the idea that when one does a thing “for love” it is for no monetary gain, the word “love” thus implying "nothing".

The former assumption that it had originated from French {{m|fr|œuf|l’œuf|lit=the egg}}, due to its shape, has largely been discredited and is no longer widely accepted. However, the apparent similarity of the shape of an egg to a zero has inspired similar analogies, such as the use of {{m|en|duck}} (reputed to be short for duck's egg) for a zero score at cricket, and {{m|en|goose egg}} for "zero".

====Noun====
{{en-noun|-}}

# {{lb|en|racquet sports|billiards}} [[zero|Zero]], no score.
#: {{ux|en|So that’s fifteen-'''love''' to Kournikova.}}
#* {{quote-text|en|year=2013|author=w:Paul McNamee|title=Game Changer: My Tennis Life
|passage=The next day [[w:Andre Agassi|Agassi]] came back from two sets to '''love''' down to beat Courier in five sets.}}
# Nothing; no recompense. <!--see Hotten's Slang Dictionary 1873-->
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1916|author=H. Rider Haggard|title=The Ivory Child
|passage=I fought the white man for less than sixpence. I fought him for '''love''', which is nothing at all.}}
